questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

As children tend to be highly impressionistic (1)/ one must be very careful for doing (2)/ or saying anything in their presence. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. Since, there are some words which take fixed preposition with them like accustomed with, careful of, obliged to, etc. Hence, replace **for **with **of. **Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **As children tend to be highly impressionistic one must be very careful of doing or saying anything in their presence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

An act of kindness (1)/ never gone (2)/ wasted. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Here, concept of simple present tense is brought under consideration. Here, a moral or universal truth is being presented. Such phrases are used in simple present tense. Also, verb's third form is used with helping verb 'has/have/had'. And, **an act of ****kindness **is described as a singular noun. So, according to sub-verb agreement, singular verb should be used. Thus, replace **gone **with **goes. **Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **An act of kindness never goes wasted.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

My daughter Meera really wants _________dog for Christmas.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of articles is brought under consideration. Since, we know article **an **is used before words starting with vowels a,e,i,o & u. Hence, option 2 is eliminated. Now, it is mentioned for a single dog.Thus, we need to emphasize on his number i.e. singular noun. Hence, option 4 is eliminated. Now, there is no specification for a particular or definite dog. It talks about any dog in the world. We know, article **the **is used for particular nouns i.e. only one. Hence, option 3 is eliminated. Thus, option 1 i.e. **a **is a correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **My daughter Meera really wants a dog for Christmas.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

A lively person is always ______ great company.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of articles is brought under consideration. Since, we know article **an **is used before words starting with vowels a,e,i,o & u. Hence, option 2 is eliminated. Now, it is mentioned for a single person. Thus, we need to emphasize on his great company which is again single. Hence, option 4 is eliminated. Now, there is no specification for a particular or definite person. It talks about all the people on this earth taking a holistic example of any single person. So, we cannot use article **the **before it. Hence, option 3 is eliminated. Thus, option 1 i.e. **a **is a correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **A lively person is always a great company.

questions.question: Students who take their studies seriously do ______ in their exams

options.text: None of the option is correct.

questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

On looking at the passage, we observe that it is based on importance of studies in a student's life for a better future. It is mentioned that students who work hard at an earlier stage in life, does not study at later life. They opt for good professions. Whereas, other who also perform well in their profession, but have to make themselves worried by studying at later life too. So, it is said that there is not shortcut or trick to success. One has to work hard for achieving success, and age does not matter to achieve success.

Word **head start **means an advantage given or gained in a competition, etc.

The starter of passage describes that students who are serious for their studies and work hard, they perform good in their exams. It is understood, more you are passionate about something, more you perform well.

**Correct sentence - **Students who take their studies seriously do well in their exams and get a head-start in life

questions.question: B is 4 years older to C. C is 6 years younger to D. D is 2 years older to E. E is 7 years younger to F. Who is the eldest?
questions.solution:
According to the given information:

1) B is 4 years older to C → B > C. Therefore, B = C + 4 

2) C is 6 years younger to D → C E. Therefore, D = E + 2

4) E is 7 years younger to F → F > E Therefore, F = E + 7

Thus, F > D > E, B > C.

Hence, F is eldest among all others.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some red are green.

II. All red are yellow.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some green are yellow.

II. Some green are not red.
questions.solution:
According to the given information:

**Statements:**

I. Some red are green.

II. All red are yellow.

__**Least Possible Venn- diagram:**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a77220c76a38b0abae44c07eebb5b4b08be20e2da5c7b806ab03c0f55584287.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some green are yellow → It is definite, hence true.

II. Some green are not red → It is possible but not definite, hence false.

Hence, only conclusion (I) follows.

***Note**: In syllogism, any condition can not be tagged as 'follows' until and unless there is not even a single possibility to negate that condition.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "WALK" is written as "46" and "TRAP" is written as "54". How is "STOP" written in that code language?

T + R + A + P = 20 + 18 + 1 + 16 = 55 - 1 = 54

Similarly,

S + T + O + P = 19 + 20 + 15 + 16 = 70 - 1 = 69

Hence, “**STOP**” can be written in that code language as “**69**”.

∴ Tank will be filled in 9 hours.

questions.question: A profit of 20% is made after giving a discount of 10% on an article. If the marked price of the article is Rs 2240, then what is its cost price (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
**Short trick∶**

Cost price = 2240 × 0.9/1.2 = Rs. 1680

**Detailed solution∶**

MP = Marked Price

SP = Selling Price

Given : MP = 2240

⇒ SP = MP - 0.1MP = 0.9MP = 0.9 × 2240 = 2016

Profit = 20%

⇒ SP = CP + 0.2CP = 1.2CP

⇒ 1.2CP = 2016

⇒ CP = 2016 / 1.2 = 1680

∴ Cost Price = Rs 1680

questions.question: An article has marked price of Rs 7500 and is available at a discount of 20%. The shopkeeper gives another discount to the buyer and sells the article for Rs 5100. What is the second discount (in %) offered?
questions.solution:
Marked Price = 7500

Initial SP after 20% discount = 7500 - 0.2 × 7500 = 6000

Final SP = 5100

Let x be final discount

⇒ Final SP = 6000 - (x / 100) × 6000 = 6000 - 60x

⇒ 5100 = 6000 - 60x

⇒ 60x = 6000 - 5100 = 900

⇒ x = 900 / 60 = 15

∴ Second Discount = 15%
